title: Sycamore Knoll undersea base claim rejected
summary: Tim Gallaudet tells of Sycamore Knoll undersea base claim rejected, about unspecified at Point Dume, Malibu, California, and summarises it without a named source. As told, not a fact.
place_text: Sycamore Knoll, off Point Dume, Southern California

tellings.quote: There was no alien base there.
we did the research and we're like I don't think there's anything

as_told.title: Michels and Will O'Brien look into a rover survey at Point Dume

related.note: Both concern the claimed alien base off Point Dume (Sycamore Knoll); the story asserts a base that was erased from maps, while this telling says there was no base.

plain: This story is about Sycamore Knoll, an undersea hill off Point Dume near Malibu in Southern California, which some have said hides an alien base under the sea. The idea is linked to a man named Preston Dennett and a book called Undersea UFO Base. A retired Navy admiral named Tim Gallaudet, speaking on the podcast of a host named Jesse Michels, says plainly that there was no alien base there. Michels backs this up from his own side, saying he and a colleague named Will O'Brien looked into it, including a survey by an underwater rover, and concluded they did not think there was anything there. So the two tellers agree, one giving an expert's view and the other his own research. It is told because it tests, and in their telling rejects, one of the best known claims of a hidden alien base in American waters.
